questions.question: Which European country sponsored many early voyages around Africa to reach Indian Ocean trade?
choices: Sweden
Portugal
Russia
Poland

questions.question: What was one major reason European states sponsored overseas exploration in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries?
choices: To end all maritime trade
To avoid contact with Asian markets
To seek trade routes, wealth, and political influence
To establish democratic governments everywhere

questions.question: What was the Columbian Exchange?
choices: A treaty that ended the American Revolution
A trade route only within the Indian Ocean
A system of European guilds
The movement of plants, animals, people, and diseases between the Americas and Afro-Eurasia

questions.question: Which crop from the Americas became an important food in many parts of Afro-Eurasia?
choices: Potato
Wheat
Olive
Rice

questions.question: What was one devastating effect of European arrival in the Americas on Indigenous populations?
choices: All Indigenous societies immediately moved to Europe
Epidemic diseases contributed to severe population loss
Disease had no effect on population
European arrival ended all warfare

questions.question: What was the encomienda system in Spanish America?
choices: A democratic election system
A form of Indigenous land ownership protected equally by law
A colonial labor system that granted Spanish settlers claims to Indigenous labor and tribute
A trade agreement between Spain and Portugal

questions.question: Why did European colonial powers increasingly transport enslaved Africans to the Americas?
choices: African labor was freely chosen in all cases
Plantations required no workers
European states sought to end racial slavery
Colonial plantation economies demanded coerced labor as Indigenous populations declined and labor needs grew

questions.question: Which treaty attempted to divide newly claimed lands outside Europe between Spain and Portugal?
choices: Treaty of Tordesillas
Treaty of Versailles
Treaty of Paris
Treaty of Utrecht

questions.question: How did mercantilist policies shape colonial economies?
choices: Colonies controlled all trade independently
Colonies were expected to supply resources and markets that benefited the home country
Mercantilism prohibited exports
European states avoided using tariffs

questions.question: Why did plantation agriculture expand in parts of the Caribbean and Brazil?
choices: The region lacked fertile land
Plantations were designed to support small farms only
European demand for sugar and other commodities encouraged large-scale production using enslaved labor
The Atlantic slave trade had ended before plantations developed

questions.question: Which statement best describes the Atlantic slave trade?
choices: A voluntary labor exchange with equal rights
A trade route that carried only European settlers
A system that ended with the first transatlantic voyage
A forced migration that transported millions of Africans to the Americas under brutal conditions

questions.question: What was one consequence of the Columbian Exchange for Afro-Eurasian populations?
choices: New staple crops contributed to population growth in some regions
All crops from the Americas failed to grow elsewhere
The exchange stopped migration
The exchange affected only sailors

questions.question: A European empire claims a territory without consulting its Indigenous inhabitants. What does this illustrate about colonialism?
choices: Colonial rule always reflected local consent
Political control and resource extraction were often imposed through unequal power
Colonialism was limited to trade without settlement
Empires avoided controlling land

questions.question: How did Indigenous peoples respond to European colonization?
choices: They all responded in the same way
They had no political choices or actions
They used varied strategies including resistance, negotiation, adaptation, and alliance
They immediately abandoned every cultural practice

questions.question: Why did control of sea routes matter to early modern European states?
choices: It made overland trade impossible everywhere
It guaranteed that ships never encountered risk
It removed competition among empires
It could influence access to trade, colonies, and naval power

questions.question: Which statement about European exploration is accurate?
choices: It expanded European knowledge and power while relying on knowledge and labor from other peoples
It was conducted without navigational technologies
It affected no societies outside Europe
It ended trade across the Indian Ocean

questions.question: Why did many colonial economies specialize in producing a small number of export crops or minerals?
choices: Colonies were required to be economically self-sufficient
Imperial demand and local conditions encouraged extraction and export of selected commodities
Exports were prohibited by mercantilism
Local consumers controlled all production decisions

questions.question: A historian analyzes ship logs, Indigenous accounts, and plantation records about colonization. Why compare these sources?
choices: Each source tells the same story from the same viewpoint
Plantation records alone represent every enslaved person's experience
They reveal different perspectives and can clarify power relations and lived experiences
Source comparison eliminates historical interpretation

questions.question: What was one long-term impact of colonial boundaries and institutions?
choices: They made every postcolonial state identical
They had no influence after independence
They eliminated all local political traditions
They shaped later political and economic conditions, though outcomes varied by place

questions.question: Why should the term 'discovery' be used carefully when describing Europeans reaching the Americas?
choices: Indigenous peoples already lived there and had their own societies and histories
No European reached the Americas
The term refers only to finding new navigational tools
Indigenous communities had no geographic knowledge
